title: We had no idea what we were getting into when we decided to make an Indian-inspired action game...
author: Treta_Studios
selftext:
A few years ago, we were just a couple of college friends who loved playing games.

Like many gamers, we always had ideas about the kind of games we wanted to see, we kept asking ourselves:

"Why don't we see more games inspired by Indian history, traditions, and warrior stories?"

So we decided to try making one ourselves.

We honestly had no idea what we were getting into.

We had to learn everything from scratch - game development, art, design, storytelling, building a world, and everything that comes with creating an indie game.

There were countless challenges, abandoned ideas, late nights, and moments where we wondered if we would actually be able to finish it.

But every small milestone kept us going.

Seeing our characters move for the first time, seeing environments come alive, and watching something that existed only in our imagination slowly become real was an incredible feeling.

After years of work, we are finally getting close to releasing Kaal Yoddha. (attaching screenshots we made and enhanced with the help of AI).

It’s an action-adventure game inspired by Indian history and traditions, but with its own original world and story.

We would love to hear your thoughts:

What kind of Indian-inspired stories or worlds would you like to see more of in games?

If you’re interested in following our journey, you can wishlist Kaal Yoddha on Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/3320200/Curse\_of\_The\_Mask\_Kaal\_Yoddha\_\_An\_Action\_Adventure\_Game/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/3320200/Curse_of_The_Mask_Kaal_Yoddha__An_Action_Adventure_Game/)

comments.author: not_varun
comments.body: You guys are using AI to make a game about Indian history? I hope you know the can of worms you’re about to open.

replies.author: not_varun
replies.body:
Apart from the usual AI bad discourse that’s going to plague them, there’s the topic of using Indian mythology as the setting. I say mythology not history because I doubt it’s going to be truly historically accurate or have fantastical elements weaved in - that’s an aside anyway.

The reaction of Indian audiences when you use mythology is going to be 100% critical because it’s seen as a cheap way of getting attention, an unimaginative setting that has been done to death, and most indie projects aim for something massively ambitious but just end up doing a bad job, angering the more zealous fans as well. 

If you want a parallel Google “Ramayana Movie 2026”, it’s an upcoming mythological movie with massive Indian stars and a massive budget, but it is plagued with criticism from every angle. There have been many renditions of the epic over time but I think the last good adaptation people could agree on was in the 90s and animated, and funnily enough, made by a Japanese artist.

replies.author: YesImYou
replies.body: So your point is “don’t make an art piece of one of the biggest and richest mythologies we have because it will offend people who are not know for their intelligence?” Bad, bad, bad

replies.author: not_varun
replies.body:
Nowhere did I say that, and nowhere did I imply people have lesser or more intelligence. I’m just warning the dev of the potential fallout and consequences. 

I’m working on a mythological setting myself so I know the kind of flak you get for even trying. If anything I wanted to start a conversation about it with the dev.

replies.author: YesImYou
replies.body: Do you know what sub this is?

replies.author: not_varun
replies.body: I didn’t say anything about AI game dev apart from the obvious, I’m here because I respect it as a process.

replies.author: not_varun
replies.body: That’s fair. It was the most glaring bit of advice but yeah I could’ve skipped it on this sub. The Indian gaming community will not take to AI very lightly because we’ve had a major gaming rug pull recently (Mumbai Gullies), and another potential one coming soon. I don’t remember what the game is called but you might know it as the one with “aura farming”.

comments.author: BestStorage6608
comments.body: Steam is not going to allow your build go live if your using enhanced screenshots.   Screenshots need to be 100% accurate to the game the player will be playing.
